target_pattern: Distinguish ir for destination, irse for departure, and salir for exiting, going out, release events, and outcome expressions like me salio bien.

cognitive_shift.english_trap: Using one leave/go translation for all movement meanings.
cognitive_shift.spanish_logic: Spanish separates movement verbs by focus: destination ir, departure irse, and exit or outcome salir.
target_pattern_formula: destination: ir plus a plus place
origin or exit: salir de plus place
social and activity: salir a plus infinitive and salir con plus person
outcome: indirect object pronoun plus salir plus adjective or adverb
natural_examples: Salgo de casa a las ocho.

pattern_mutation.instructions: Transform each base sentence as instructed.
drills: Base: Voy a la tienda. -> change destination to el banco.
Base: Me voy ahora. -> change subject to plural nosotros.
Base: Salgo de la casa a las ocho. -> change place to la oficina.
Base: Maria se fue a Estados Unidos. -> change destination to Espana.
Base: Quieres salir a cenar? -> change infinitive to caminar.
Base: Mi ex sale con mi mejor amigo. -> change subject to plural mis amigos.
Base: Cuanto tiempo llevan saliendo? -> change to singular ella with tu primo.
Base: La nueva pelicula sale en junio. -> change month to septiembre.
Base: El informe salio mejor de lo esperado. -> change adjective to peor.
Base: El examen me salio dificil. -> change pronoun to nos.
Base: Como te salio la entrevista? -> change noun to presentacion.
Base: Vete. -> change to formal imperative positive.
Base: No te vayas. -> change to formal negative command.
Base: Se va ahora. -> change to first person singular.
Base: Salimos a cenar esta noche. -> change to yesterday past form.

prompts: I am going to the office. (Voy a la oficina. vs Me voy la oficina.)
I am leaving now. (Me voy ahora. vs Voy ahora.)
I leave the house at seven. (Salgo de la casa a las siete. vs Me voy de la casa a las siete.)
Maria headed out to Peru. (Maria se fue a Peru. vs Maria fue a Peru.)
What time does the bus leave? (A que hora sale el autobus? vs A que hora se va el autobus?)
Do you want to go out to eat? (Quieres salir a comer? vs Quieres irse a comer?)
She is dating Juan. (Ella sale con Juan. vs Ella va con Juan.)
The movie comes out in May. (La pelicula sale en mayo. vs La pelicula va en mayo.)
The exam went badly for me. (El examen me salio mal. vs El examen fui mal.)
How did the meeting go for you? (Como te salio la reunion? vs Como te fue la reunion?)

common_errors.mistake: Ir used when departure meaning is intended
common_errors.why_it_happens: English go covers both destination and leaving.

common_errors.correct_spanish: Use me voy te vas se va and related forms.

common_errors.mistake: Salir overused for all movement contexts
common_errors.correct_spanish: Choose verb by focus destination departure exit or outcome.

common_errors.mistake: Voy de casa used for leaving a place habitually
Salir a plus infinitive confused with ir a plus infinitive
common_errors.correct_spanish: Salir a means go out to do something.

common_errors.why_it_happens: Salir learned only as physical movement.
common_errors.correct_spanish: Use me te le salio bien mal dificil and similar patterns.

common_errors.why_it_happens: Pronoun placement and command forms mixed.
common_errors.correct_spanish: Use vete vayase no te vayas no se vaya.

common_errors.mistake: Ir used for media release dates
common_errors.why_it_happens: Confusion from English come out phrasing.

common_errors.mistake: Fue and salio treated as identical outcome expressions
common_errors.correct_spanish: High-frequency outcome frame is me salio bien or mal.
